title: scheduler executor configuration
description: The host half of the scheduler (SPEC-16.G g-executor): its socket, host paths, the seat the record verb forces, and the verb table of SPEC-16.H h-verbs. Every key is required and no other key is allowed, because Go holds no default. The verbs object takes exactly the names the scheduler emits: a verb missing here blocks going active (g-val-verbs), and an extra name is surface nobody asked for (h-examples, no shell verb). argv is a token list, never a command line, so nothing is parsed by a shell. In a token, ${host_repo}, ${state_dir}, ${session} (herdr_session) and ${seat} come from this file at load; ${1} to ${9} bind the Run arguments by position and ${@} binds the remaining arguments, which only the record verb uses. final lists the exit codes that are handled results; it is required even when empty, because an absent list would be a default. No $schema keyword, for the reason scheduler.schema.json gives.

path.description: a host path that starts with a variable, so the file lifts to another host unchanged

token.description: one argv token; a variable outside the set above is refused here rather than at the first run

flags.description: the writer flags the scheduler may pass (h-verbs-record-flags); seat is not in the enum, so the scheduler can never override the forced seat

socket.description: the unix socket the executor listens on with mode 0600, under the runtime directory variable (h-proto-sockets)

host_repo.description: the repository on the host; COQ_REPO, as the host shell names it

state_dir.description: herdr's state dir, where seats/<seat>/quiet.json and the inbox live (SPEC-05 s-quiet); the same place herdr/config/herdr.json state_dir names

herdr_session.description: the session every herdr verb addresses; same variable as scheduler.json herdr_session

seat.description: forced on every record the record verb writes; must equal scheduler.json seat

tail_lines.description: lines of stdout and stderr returned in a verdict

unset_env.description: removed before every verb so a herdr call never targets the executor's own pane; the four names factory/bin/route.sh herdr_prompt unsets today
